answers.answer: Set out players + 1 Factory cards face-down; return extras unseen. Place one encounter token on each of 11 marked territories and randomly select one structure bonus tile face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.

Starting pieces: character at home base; two workers on the two land-adjoined territories beside it; four mechs over Faction Mat abilities; six stars by faction emblem; six tech cubes in black-square green boxes; structures/recruits on matching Player Mat spaces; remaining six workers on Produce red rectangles; action token beside Player Mat. Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; Player Mat sets popularity, coins, and two objectives.

You must move token to a different section, but may take neither action (dead turn) or either/both. Rusviet may repeat a section; top and bottom each still once, and bottom must follow top. Top-row gains may pay bottom costs. Pay full exposed red-box costs; choose any or all exposed green-box benefits. Exact bottom cost/coins depend on mat/upgrades.

Enemy worker alone on your structure territory controls it and its resources; the enemy does not gain your structure ability, and you retain it (except Mill production requires control). Pay resources from any territories you currently control, even for an action elsewhere.

Normal Move selects up to two different units, one adjacent territory each; one unit cannot move twice from the two selections. Mechs carry your workers, not your character; all units can carry resources. A transported worker’s carried movement does not count as its own, so it may subsequently move itself.

Mech entering territory with enemy workers only stops and cannot move again that turn; those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leave resources, and you lose one popularity per worker down to zero (retreat still happens at zero). Your workers cannot independently enter while enemy workers control it.

After all units finish a Move action, combat occurs before the following bottom action; attacker chooses multiple-combat order. Workers cannot independently move into or out of territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.

Bolster costs $1: gain 2 power or 1 combat card. If deck empty, shuffle discards; if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1: gain any 2 resources or 1 popularity. Traded resources go on a controlled territory with at least one worker; cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are home.

Produce requires paying all exposed power/popularity/coin costs in full before production. Then select up to two different controlled territories; each worker there may produce one terrain-matching token. New workers come left-to-right from Player Mat and go in producing village. Benefits, including worker production, may be declined; newly exposed costs affect future Produce actions, not cost already paid.

Upgrade pays exposed oil cost; move a tech cube from green box to an empty bracketed red box (not solid-black-bordered), improving top benefit/reducing bottom cost. Deploy pays exposed metal cost; place a mech on a controlled territory with your worker, never lake; uncovered ability applies to character and all mechs, not workers. Even when upgrades/mechs/etc. are complete, you may still pay a bottom action for coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonuses.

Build a structure on a controlled territory with your worker; one structure total per territory, Factory allowed, lakes/home bases forbidden. Structures cannot move or be destroyed. Mill only produces while controlled, with its bonus production territory and worker output; Mine gives personal tunnel movement even when enemy-controlled. Enemy occupants do not grant/use your building ability.

Enlist: take a recruit from any bottom-row section and permanently place on any open one-time Faction Mat bonus, immediately taking 2 power, 2 coins, 2 popularity, or 2 combat cards; token cannot move. Ongoing bonus comes from circle uncovered where recruit was removed. On bottom actions, active player resolves first, then immediate left, then right; stop at sixth star. Two-player opponent triggers once. Exact simultaneous recruit-star sequence is specified for power/popularity recruit bonuses: active action first, then active, left, right, checking game end.

Combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power 0 through min(7,current power), plus optionally one card per participating character/mech (People’s Army adds one card if any worker present). Reveal simultaneously; add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Combat abilities: attacker’s first, then defender’s. Both pay selected dial power from track and discard played cards face-up.

Winner controls territory/resources. Losing characters, mechs, and workers retreat to home base (eligible Nordic Seaworthy retreat may go to adjacent lake), leaving all resources. Winning attacker loses 1 popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, including workers carried by defeated mech on lake; defender loses none. Combat star per limits: non-Saxony winner with zero/one combat stars places one; with two places none; Saxony places one each victory if star available. Loser draws one combat card if revealed any dial power or card value; zero-total loser gets none.

After whole Move action and all combats, if character remains on encounter, discard token and draw before following bottom action; if character loses contested entry and retreats, token remains. Gains are placed on encounter territory. No additional normal action costs or mat benefits/recruit bonuses apply. (Summary states these details; question’s “when” is after combats.)

Every player’s character, on its first finish of a Move action at Factory (after winning combat if needed), chooses one available Factory card; return rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card; later visits cannot exchange. Card is fifth section with optional top then bottom and usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception); Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses, or ongoing recruits. Factory bottom Move moves one unit up to two territories, three if character/mech with Speed; normal restrictions apply.

Only on own turn, before or after completing top/bottom action, may reveal completed objective; must meet all requirements at reveal. Put star and both objective cards on bottom of deck. Normally one objective star; Saxony may complete both starting objectives, keeping second card after first.

Stars for six upgrades, four mechs, four structures, four recruits, all eight workers on board, one revealed completed objective, combat victory (up to two stars except Saxony), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Stars permanent; another player’s stars do not block goals. Sixth star immediately ends play.

If bottom action earns sixth star, first collect primary benefit, coins and your ongoing recruit benefit, then place star. Pending intermingled battles are undone by returning initiating units to territories they came from; don’t resolve another combat. Neighbor recruit-star sequence: finish active action, active player then left then right; if sixth star earlier, later recruit star/bonus does not resolve.

At popularity 10, star tier is $4 each: 5 stars = $20. Territory tier is $3 per counted territory: 4 normal territories plus Factory counted as 3 = 7, or $21. Resource tier is $2 per complete pair: 13 resources = 6 pairs = $12 (one leftover ignored). Add held coins and eligible selected structure bonus; structures qualify even if enemies control their territories, but payout cannot be determined without selected tile/features. Tiebreakers: workers+mechs+structures, power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, stars placed.

Home base is not a territory for any game effect; normally cannot move into one (setup/forced retreat exceptions; Crimea Wayfare exception). Bases without matching core factions are inactive expansion placeholders.
Mountain=metal, tundra=oil, farm=food, forest=wood, village=worker; lake and Factory produce nothing. Workers are not resources. Resource tokens have no supply limit; use multipliers if needed.
answers.evidence: Produce; Control, resources and home bases

answers.answer: Any unit may pick up/carry/drop resources mid-movement; only mechs carry your workers, never character. Speed adds one territory to each selected character/mech, not worker; tunnel jump costs one step and additional step may be before/after. Mech can pick up/drop resources/workers mid-movement. Enemy-unit and encounter stops override Speed.
Yes, any unit may enter territory with enemy structure only, taking control without combat. All printed tunnel territories are adjacent for movement by any unit.
You cannot pay partial cost. If unable to afford any action, legal dead turn: move token to a different section and take neither action.

Armory grants +1 power on Trade; Monument grants +1 popularity on Bolster. Structure benefits apply on matching actions; you retain abilities even without control, except Mill cannot produce on uncontrolled territory. Enemy units do not gain your structure abilities.

Unlocked Riverwalk lets character and all mechs cross rivers to faction-specific terrain, not workers: Nordic/Saxony forests and mountains; Rusviet farms and villages; Crimea farms and tundra; Polania villages and mountains. Nordic Swim is separate: workers alone cross rivers to any land terrain, not lakes; it does not give mechs lake movement.

Saxony Underpass: controlled mountains and all tunnels (including own Mine) adjacent for character/mech Move. Rusviet Township: controlled villages and Factory adjacent for character/mech Move. Other unit eligibility is not granted by these abilities.

Saxony Disarm applies before combat on tunnel or own Mine: opponent loses 2 power on track, once per combat, not per unit. Nordic Artillery differs: may pay 1 power before combat to reduce opponent power by 2, once per combat, not per unit.

People’s Army gives one additional combat card total in combat with at least one worker, while still requiring a character/mech. Two mechs plus three workers may play three cards. Workers alone never fight.
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities; Combat

answers.answer: Crimea Wayfare lets character/mechs move from territory or home base to own or any inactive faction home base regardless of distance; cannot enter active opponent home base.

Crimea Scout steals one random opponent combat card into your hand before combat, once per combat, not per unit. Coercion once per turn spends one combat card as any one resource, regardless of card value.

Nordic Seaworthy: character/mechs move to/from lakes and may retreat to adjacent lake instead of home; mechs may carry workers. Polania Submerge: character/mechs move to/from lakes and from any lake to any other lake; no adjacent-lake retreat exception stated. With either, workers on lakes need a mech to move off; cannot leave carried workers or resources behind when carrier leaves.
Camaraderie prevents popularity loss for opposing workers forced to retreat after you win combat as aggressor on your turn. It does not cover loss for driving out undefended workers without combat.

Meander lets Polania choose up to two different options on one encounter card, in either order; first gain can pay second cost. Summary does not specify a distinct card count or further payment mechanism beyond paying printed costs and taking as little benefit as desired. Unsupported: exact special card-count detail beyond “one encounter card.”
answers.evidence: Faction and unlocked mech abilities; Encounters

answers.answer: Character reaching encounter token stops and cannot move again that turn. Encounter resolves after whole Move action and all combats, if character remains; applies during Factory Move too.

Coin values need not be revealed when asked (coins are not hidden information). Combat card hand count public, though during combat may conceal whether any cards were committed until reveal; card contents secret until revealed. Objective contents secret until completed objective revealed.

Only coins are tangible items exchangeable; agreements informal and unenforceable; tournament play even forbids coin exchanges for deals/alliances. A payment cannot cancel combat initiated by movement; combat proceeds after Move (bribes may influence outcome).

Popularity 0–6: stars $3 each, territories $2 each, resource pairs $1; 7–12: $4, $3, $2; 13–18: $5, $4, $3. Factory counts as 3 territories; controlled lakes count, home bases do not. Score complete pairs of controlled resources only; leftover single does not score.

Adjacency tiles count unique features across all structures: printed tunnels (not Mines), lakes, and printed encounter locations even after token removed. Payout by count: tunnels 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6=$9; lakes 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9; encounters 1=$2, 2–3=$4, 4–5=$6, 6–7=$9. Rivers do not break adjacency.

Structures-on-tunnels counts printed tunnel territories, not Mines: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3–4=$6. Structures-in-a-row scores only longest continuous straight line; rivers do not break it: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9. Farm/tundra tile counts combined qualifying structures: 1=$2, 2=$4, 3=$6, 4=$9.
Yes. Winning attacker loses one popularity for each enemy worker forced to retreat, even workers carried by defeated mech on lake.

Star is permanent if popularity later drops, but current popularity determines final scoring tier; star does not lock tier. Other players’ stars never block a goal, so two factions may each star same achievement.

Randomly deal each player one Faction Mat and one Player Mat. Seat factions clockwise in board order Nordic, Rusviet, Crimea, Saxony, Polania, omitting inactive factions. Seating matters because ongoing recruit bonuses trigger for active player and immediate left/right neighbors.

River is border between two land territories; lake occupies whole hex and extends to each adjacent shoreline. A unit with applicable lake movement may enter from any surrounding land territory adjoining those shores.
No: show encounter card to all players when drawn, show artwork, and read capitalized thematic text aloud; need not read every option aloud.
No limit on friendly units or resource tokens on a territory.
After current player starts a noninteractive bottom-row action, next clockwise player may begin while current player decides which upgrade, mech, structure or recruit to gain.
No. Each chosen top and bottom action limited to once in turn, including Rusviet; Rusviet repetition only waives previous-turn section restriction.
Normal Move alternative is gain $1 instead of moving units.
No. Workers never return to Player Mat, including after retreat; retreat sends them to home base.
Yes. You may attack with zero power, zero popularity, or both.
Yes. You may still fight after reaching combat-star limit; non-Saxony winner with two combat stars places no more combat stars.
For faction without Meander, must choose one affordable option; cannot decline all or choose unaffordable coin/popularity option. May take as little of chosen benefit as desired.
No turn-order selection: both simultaneously and secretly choose dial and optional cards. Reveal simultaneously.
Announce the bottom-row action so neighbors can check recruit bonuses.

Place star as soon as goal achieved; sixth star ends game immediately. By contrast, completed objective may be held and revealed later, but only on own turn before/after action and while meeting all requirements.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end; Objectives and agreements

answers.answer: Normally units cannot cross rivers or enter lakes; faction/mech abilities provide exceptions.
No. Recruit token is permanently placed on Faction Mat one-time bonus and cannot later move.
No. Only character triggers encounter; character entering stops and encounter resolves after Move and combats if remains.

Controlled Mill adds one bonus territory to current Produce allowance: two normal choices become up to three; upgraded allowance of three becomes up to four. Mill itself counts as one producing worker even without actual worker; each actual worker at Mill also produces normally, so Mill output adds to worker output. Mill only works while controlled.
Control by having a unit there, or your structure there with no enemy unit. Resources alone do not establish/preserve control after last unit leaves when no structure there.
Build uses wood; Enlist uses food.
